text:
A small team has few communication paths. Members talk to each other directly and do not wait for meetings or reports. A small team does not need a meeting for most choices. A large team has many more paths between people. Each new person adds more connections, and coordination takes more time.

A small team also has fewer approval steps. One person can decide and act. A large team often needs sign-off from several managers before work continues. This approval step adds delay between a decision and a result.

A small team owns its work from start to end. Each member sees the full result of a change and can fix a problem fast. A large team splits work among many groups. A problem in one part can wait for another group to respond.

Small size removes overhead. Large size adds it. This difference is why small teams ship faster.
